children: HPE stock was falling on Thursday despite signs of continued demand strength as Wall Street weighed whether they think the company can overcome margin pressures and supply headwinds.

HPE reported better-than-expected fiscal third-quarter financial results after the stock market closed on Wednesday. The information technology company also raised its guidance for the full year, and CEO Antonio Neri told Barron's that demand is incredibly strong as customers continue to build out the infrastructure needed to power artificial intelligence.

"Similar to Dell's report, the better guidance reflects continued momentum from AI servers, with traditional servers and storage now also contributing to the better top-line growth," Raymond James analyst Simon Leopold wrote on Thursday. He raised his price target on HPE to $86 from $74 while maintaining an Outprform rating on the stock.
Despite the strong results, shares were down 7.1% to $48.15.
Wall Street was worried about HPE management's commentary regarding margins and supply constraints.

CFO Marie Myers said on the earnings call that HPE expects its operating margin rate to "decline sequentially, driven primarily by a higher mix of AI systems in Cloud & AI and pricing." Essentially, while demand for AI systems is incredibly high, the margins on these products are limited because of the high costs of components like graphic processing units, or GPUs.

Demand for HPE's offerings is also far outpacing supply. HPE said on its earnings call that these supply constraints have limited the company's ability to convert higher demand into revenue in the quarter.

"Supply remains a constraint, but others have been better able to get supply," Piper Sandler analyst James Fish wrote on Wednesday night. "We continue to prefer others in the space." Fish rates HPE as Neutral with a $57 price target.

Other analysts are more optimistic. Evercore ISI's Amit Daryanani wrote in a note that while supply issues remain an investor concern, "HPE said it has more than doubled its networking supply commitments and expects supply availability to become better aligned with order bookings starting in FQ4." He maintained an Outperform rating and lowered his price target to $65 from $70.
